A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeurGrad/NEG and MCEval8K research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original neuron-intervention experiments, gradient-estimation comparisons and MCEval8K skill-probing results, including extensive appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports revised neuron-intervention results, new attribution and multi-neuron experiments, and retained MCEval8K probing outcomes.

M1.justification: Equation (1) changes from GC × −sign(A) to CG × sign(A), reversing the documented estimator's polarity. v2 also removes the random-forest Tree-prober, retaining the two majority-vote probers. The PDFs do not establish whether the sign revision reflects an implementation change or a correction to the written formula.

E1.justification: Both use MyriadLAMA for single-token factual probing and the same 22 MCEval8K tasks across six genres and five languages. The additional models and intervention analyses use the existing factual prompts and language-task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Log-Probability-Increase (LPI; Yu and Ananiadou, 2024) alongside computational and integrated gradients, reporting Llama2-7B/13B comparisons in Table 1. Across MCEval8K, the Tree-prober comparison is removed, while Rand, LM-Prob and the majority-vote probers remain.

E3.justification: Figure 2 changes from random/top-gradient comparisons on six models to random-neuron evaluation on nine, adding pretrained Llama2-7B/13B and Phi3-mini. v2 introduces MAE/timing evaluation, top-K attribution interventions and multi-neuron sweeps up to 4096 neurons. Its Table 4 caption still specifies top-gradient sampling, leaving that table's selection protocol inconsistent with the main text.

E4.justification: v2 Section 5.2 and Appendix D add sensitivity tests over neuron counts and activation-shift ranges; Appendix B.1 adds activation-distribution analysis. v1's Tree-prober depth/tree-count analyses, decision-tree case study and gradient-noise analysis are removed. Efficiency, context-generality and neuron-subset analyses are retained in the appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both use descriptive averages, neuron-distribution statistics and range displays; v2 does not document a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises correlations, including NeurGrad's Llama2-7B value from 0.9769 to 0.8136 and Llama2-70B from 0.7811 to 1.000, and adds MAE/runtime results. Linearity statistics change, and attribution/multi-neuron findings are added. Tree-prober results disappear; retained baseline and majority-vote entries in all 44 MCEval8K task-setting rows match. Revised results do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Section 5.3 formalizes the model as a function of neuron activations and introduces a first-order Taylor approximation for small perturbations, providing a new mathematical argument for local linearity. The NEG regression, probing objectives and generality definitions remain; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds connecting controllability with skill representation and claims four skill-neuron properties, including interdependency. v2 makes global coverage across neurons and quantitative output control central, adds multi-neuron accumulation to the introduction's findings, and drops interdependency as a contribution. NEG, NeurGrad and MCEval8K remain core contributions.

C2.justification: The Dynamic Knowledge Store Hypothesis in v1 Section 3.2 is removed. v2 introduces a local-linear explanation and qualifies multi-neuron predictability by intervention size and neuron count. It also explains attribution advantages through handling negative neurons. Existing limitations concerning single-token factual probing and untested skill-level editing remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds RTX A6000 timing hardware, LPI implementation provenance/restrictions, and model identifiers and architecture counts for additional models. It removes Tree-prober's scikit-learn implementation/defaults and the earlier numerical-precision and zero-activation disclosures. Benchmark construction, prompts and the stated data/code release link remain.

R1.justification: Related work is refocused from broad mechanistic interpretability, attention and circuits toward quantitative neuron attribution and output control. v2 adds Chen et al. (2023), Lee et al. (2024), Lundstrom et al. (2022), and editing/bias references while removing substantial attention/circuit coverage. Prior methods are increasingly positioned as relative-ranking tools lacking direct quantitative control.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around three research questions. Related Work moves from Section 7 to Section 2, linearity/estimation/controllability receive separate sections, and most skill-neuron property discussions move to Appendix H. This substantially reorganizes the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn vertically and moved to the first page; Figure 2 is redesigned, and Table 1 expands with LPI, MAE and runtime columns/rows. Attribution, multi-neuron and distribution plots are added, while Tree-prober visuals are removed. Retained analyses relocate, and the two MCEval8K result tables expand onto separate pages.

improvement.justification: v1's correlation-only estimator evaluation and qualitative efficiency argument are strengthened by absolute-error/runtime measurements, direct attribution interventions and multi-neuron sensitivity tests in v2 (Table 1, Sections 4.3–5.2, Appendices C–D). These substantially improve evidence for actual output control and clarify its limits. Removing Tree-prober narrows the skill-probing evidence, and inconsistent sampling descriptions weaken reproducibility, but the gains to validation of the central contribution outweigh these limitations.
